page.layout: One column of running text. Marginal notes in the right margin. No left margin notes.

main_text.p: more Persarum,ulli vi-ro aut fæ-mina.{a} reginæ introire ad regè, nisi accersitæ, non licet: nec tamen,b addit. a Sulpicio ut videtur.{b} quū fuerit regi libitum, sed statuto tempore admittitur) & forte tum ita evenerat, ut diebus triginta proximis separata a con-spectu regis Hester haberetur. Igitur audendum aliquid pro civibus rata, etsi certa pestis adesset, pulchro in negocio occumbere parat: invocato prius Domino, c atrium interius.{c} auiam[?] regis ingreditur. At barbarus re-infolita perculsus, paulatim blandimento muliebri delinitus: postremo ad coenam reginæ perducitur: unaque cum illo Haman ille regi charus, & ludæ{d} gentis in-festus.d gentis. Gal. Igitur quum jam post epulas multis poculis convivium calere coepisset, Hester genibus regis advolvitur, getis[?] suæ perniciem deprecatur.Esther 7. Rex vero nihil{e} a se petenti, si quid ultra peteret, negatum pollicetur.e a sepe-tenti, idem[?]. Tum Hester arrepto tempore,{f} Hamanis mortem flagitat, in ultionem gentis, quam perditam cupie-rat.f confiss[?] a Severo. Sed rex amici memor, paulisper cunctatur: deliberandiqué gratia modicum secessit. Deinde regressus, vidit Haman reginæ genua complexum: succen-sus ira, & s[?] appetitam reginam clamitans,g adst.

page.notes: Right-margin notes are abbreviated and partly illegible in the scan; readings marked [?] are doubtful. "auiam[?]" is probably "aulam" but printed as shown. "getis[?]" is uncertain (possibly gentis). The first note letter after "Persarum," is "a"; the marks "{d}" and "{f}" are reconstructed from their positions. The word after "& s[?]" is unclear. The catchword "morte" stands alone at the right below the last line.
